summary.headline: Hy-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR430 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.6% from 21.5%, which management attributes to a price-revision lag.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September 2026 listing on NSE and BSE. Revenue from operations was INR430 million (+13% YoY), EBITDA was INR84 million (vs INR82 million), and PAT was INR46 million (+11% YoY), giving a 10.7% PAT margin. Management said a raw-material price revision agreed with OEMs (effective 1 April) will only be recognised from Q2, so margin pressure is timing-related. Management guided to about 20% revenue growth, 25-30% PAT growth and a 24-25% EBITDA margin for FY27, but the call contained few hard disclosures on order book, capex scope or the planned land purchase.

segments.name: Domestic (non-export)
segments.commentary: Management put domestic revenue at about INR120-130 crore currently, and expects it to double in 3-4 years. Domestic growth is targeted at 15-20%, versus about 7-8% for the Indian industry.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export is about 25-30% of revenue, with USA about 25% and Europe about 7-8%. Management cited about 10% higher margins on export and a plan for 50% export share within 5 years.

segments.name: Distributors
segments.commentary: Four Indian distributors (Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Delhi, Pune) account for about 10% of business.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of at least 20% YoY in FY27, with a little more in each of the following two years.
PAT growth of 25-30% YoY; EBITDA margin about 24-25% for FY27, rising 0.5-1% a year over 2-3 years.
Price revision recovered from OEMs (effective 1 April) expected to reflect in Q2 FY27; management said Q1 margin was affected by this timing.
Target of roughly doubling turnover in 3 years, with capacity from 35 lakh to 70 lakh fittings per month (a later remark said 50 lakh).
Five-year target of about INR500 crore revenue, per the management response to an analyst's question.
Railway (IRIS) and defence (DRDO) business expected to contribute 1-2 years out, on top of the 20% base growth.
capex_capacity: Current capacity: about 35 lakh fittings/month across six plants (two in Shirwal near Pune, Pithampur (two), Nashik and Thane). Capacity at ~60-70% utilisation.
INR30 crore capex in FY27 to add rotary transfer machines (two installed, four more planned; each about 70,000 pieces/month, single operator). Implementation within one year.
Board approved purchase of 6.5 acres for future plant; land acquisition in 3-4 months. Plant planned in about two years, cost indicated at INR350-500 crore, to be detailed in November.
Forging: two mechanical presses (one at Shirwal, one landing at Nashik); forging capacity 15-20% above current need.
Total land: about 8 acres (320,000 sq ft) across current units.
A US 100% subsidiary and warehouse are being set up. The board sanctioned the entity today.
demand_pricing: Customers: about 170 direct customers, more than 7 active distributors, presence in 11 countries. OEM business is 70-80% of revenue; about 80% of the product range is standard.
No single customer exceeds 15% of business. Some OEMs (Windsor, John Deere) buy 100% from Hy-Tech, others 10-70%. About 2-3 new OEMs are added each year.
Pricing: management said Parker fittings are about double Hy-Tech's price. It sees no Chinese competition locally. Second domestic competitor has less than half Hy-Tech's turnover.
Management put the global fittings market at about INR40,000 crore (USA 20,000, Europe 10,000, India 2,000, other 8,000 crore).
Pass-through: management said OEMs compensate raw-material and other cost increases under informal long-term arrangements, typically within 3-6 months.
Order book: none disclosed. Management said OEMs issue annual schedules against contract orders with price.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin fall, and what FY27 margin should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 24-25% EBITDA margin for FY27. It attributed Q1 weakness to input costs rising in Feb-April, with the price revision only effective 1 April and recognised from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and PAT growth guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 20% revenue growth and 25-30% PAT growth each year, with the company citing operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30 crore of capex this year on rotary transfer machines, implemented within a year. Plant capacity would go from 35 to 50 lakh pieces/month on this, with a 6.5-acre land purchase for a later expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Mazagon Dock and Cochin Shipyard registrations generate revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Registration took about a year. Revenue may start in about 5-6 months, but management cannot guarantee timing and said it will not matter much for growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data center opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless steel fittings for data centres were developed in the last 1.5-2 years. Entry is expected over about a year, with meaningful revenue more likely in FY28-29; no specific customer enquiries yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much is spent on R&D, and will it increase?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 1% of revenue. Management said this is sufficient for standard products, and valves are being considered without commitment.

qa_highlights.question: How is the US concentration managed?
qa_highlights.answer: US is held at about 25% of revenue deliberately. Export is to reach 50% in 5 years, spread across Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Dubai. Management declined to name US or European clients.

risks_watch: Q1 margin recovery relies on the OEM price revision being recognised in Q2; management did not give a quantum.
Targets (20% revenue, 25-30% PAT, 24-25% margin) are management's own; the call gave no order book or quantified backlog.
Land purchase and plant investment (INR350-500 crore, 2-3 years out) are not yet detailed; the cost is to be disclosed in November.
Mismatch in SKU additions: new SKUs fell from about 2,206 in FY24 to about 880 in FY26 (per analyst citing RHP). Management attributed this to OEM RFQ timing.
Employee cost (about 12% of sales) and the Q1 cut-off sales shift to Q2 both affect the comparison.
Dependence on USA (about 25% of revenue) and tariff exposure. Management said it aims to diversify.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the OEM relationship, but noticeably defensive on Q1 margins, which management pinned on timing and price pass-through. Several answers were vague or deferred (land cost, plant detail, data-centre timing, US customer names), and some figures were inconsistent (capacity 50 vs 70 lakh pieces, employee-cost explanation).

growth.why: Management guided to at least 20% revenue growth and 25-30% PAT growth in FY27, backed partly by INR30 crore rotary transfer machines in trials, forging presses and a planned 6.5-acre plant (INR350-500 crore, about two years out), but no order book was disclosed and utilisation is about 65%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 24-25% EBITDA margin for FY27 versus 19.6% in Q1, with the OEM price revision (effective 1 April) expected to be recognised from Q2, though no quantum was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR30 crore rotary transfer machines (two installed, four more planned, ~70,000 pieces/month each) are in trials with implementation within a year, and forging presses are under construction; utilisation is about 65%, so this is near-term capacity rather than a new plant.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided at least 20% revenue growth in FY27 backed by OEM relationships and 2-3 new OEMs a year, but no order book was disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved a 6.5-acre purchase with land acquisition in 3-4 months and plant cost of INR350-500 crore to be detailed in November; utilisation is only about 65%, so the plant is not urgently needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is 20% revenue growth, 25-30% PAT growth and 24-25% EBITDA margin, but no order book was disclosed and Q1 EBITDA margin was 19.6%, so there is no evidence yet to raise targets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 margin of 19.6% is well below the 24-25% FY27 target and depends on the unquantified OEM price revision being recognised in Q2; targets are management's own with no backlog cover.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Stainless steel data-centre fittings were developed over the last 1.5-2 years with entry expected over about a year, but there are no customer enquiries yet and meaningful revenue is more likely in FY28-29; valves are considered without commitment.

rows.label: US subsidiary and warehouse; export share to 50% in 5 years
rows.why: Board sanctioned a US 100% subsidiary and warehouse today; export is 25-30% of revenue with about 10% higher margin, and management targets 50% export share within 5 years.

rows.label: Railway (IRIS) and defence (DRDO) business
rows.why: Management expects these to contribute 1-2 years out on top of base growth, but no order or registration quantum was disclosed; Mazagon Dock and Cochin Shipyard revenue may start in about 5-6 months with no timing guarantee.

rows.label: Forging capacity and rotary machines reducing labour per unit
rows.why: Each rotary transfer machine needs one operator for ~70,000 pieces/month, and forging capacity is 15-20% above current need, but the employee cost was about 12% of sales with absolute cost up YoY.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth, the OEM relationship and export strategy but defensive on Q1 margins, pinning them on price-revision timing; analysts pressed on the capex scope, land cost, order book and inconsistent capacity figures (50 vs 70 lakh pieces).
